correctness.rationale: Writing r_i and c_j for row and column label sums makes the zero-cell condition exactly r_i+c_j=2. This gives the lower bounds and equality classification without an unproved structural lemma. In a rectangular optimum, the presence of a zero column forces every row sum to two and every positive column to be full, yielding the two column-supported families. If all columns are positive, every row is positive; any row of sum at least two must be full, and the equality budget forces n=m+1 and exactly one such row. The remaining zero-cell equations force all other row supports into one common column. Converses are checked directly. A bounded-weight exhaustive verifier finds no lower solution and recovers exactly the stated minima on seven small instances.

value.rationale: The published product theorem settles only the scalar optimum, leaving a natural equality-structure question. The complete classification exposes a sharp optimizer phase transition: permutation matrices in the square case, column-supported minima for n>=m+2, and an additional row-column-cross family exactly at n=m+1. The factorial and closed rectangular counts are mathematically natural enumerative data, not arbitrary finite computations.
